text:
mara: FYI customer (Acme) escalated — tool call keeps failing only from Go SDK. Python/TS ok.
I can reproduce locally, error from runtime: "schema_error: args must be object, got string". Ticket #INC-4721.

mara: Repro steps:
1) Call tools.lookup_user with arg payload containing a []byte field (avatar_bytes)
2) Go SDK sends the request, runtime responds 400
3) Same payload via curl/python works.

mara: Minimal payload we used:
```json
{
  "tool": "lookup_user",
  "args": { "username": "alice", "avatar_bytes": "\u0000\u0001\u0002" }
}
```
(note: the raw field is binary in the app; we represented as escaped nulls here)

diego: can you paste the raw request body and the api_request_id from logs? also which go sdk commit?

mara: api_request_id: req_2026-03-01_6b1f9c. Raw body we see in ingress (from go client):
```json
{"tool":"lookup_user","arguments":"{\"username\":\"alice\",\"avatar_bytes\":\"\\u0000\\u0001\\u0002\"}"}
```
Notice `arguments` is a string containing JSON. From python client it's sent as a nested object: 
```json
{"tool":"lookup_user","arguments":{"username":"alice","avatar_bytes":"\u0000\u0001\u0002"}}
```

tara: ah — runtime expects `arguments` to be JSON object/array per tool schema. If Go is serializing the arguments field as a string we hit schema validation. Why would go do that?

jordan: my guess: the Go SDK's marshaller for the ToolCall type has `Arguments` typed as `interface{}` but somewhere we run `json.Marshal` twice (or accidentally call `string()` on the marshalled bytes) so it becomes a string. I've seen this with naive wrappers around encoding/json.

samira: customer impact? they hit this in prod intermittently, so we need a hotfix for the SDK and a workaround for them.

mara: impact: 40% of tool calls erroring in their integration. The customer is blocked for a feature flag rollout.

diego: thanks. quick triage — two avenues: 1) patch Go SDK to avoid double-encoding arguments, add test for nested raw json/bytes, 2) runtime can tolerate stringified arguments by attempting to parse when schema validation fails (best-effort fallback). I'll take SDK patch.

diego: repro locally: small snippet from the failing Go client shows the bug:
```go
type ToolCall struct {
  Tool string `json:"tool"`
  Arguments interface{} `json:"arguments"`
}
// bug: we do payload.Arguments = string(b) where b is json.Marshal(args)
// causing arguments to be a string of JSON
```

tara: runtime-side fallback seems safe to add (try json.Unmarshal if arguments is string). I'll add a short-term lenient parse path behind a feature flag.

mara: customer asked for workaround they can apply now. Any suggestions?

diego: quick workaround for them: construct arguments as a map[string]any and pass it directly, avoid passing pre-marshalled []byte-as-string. If they must send binary, base64-encode that field explicitly and update tool schema to expect string/base64. Share code snippet for Go: 
```go
args := map[string]any{"username":"alice","avatar_bytes": base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(raw)}
call := ToolCall{Tool: "lookup_user", Arguments: args}
// json.Marshal(call) -> correct nested object
```

samira: great. please add the workaround to the support ticket and ping the customer. Also log actions: SDK patch (diego), runtime fallback (tara), add unit tests (diego & tara), and update docs about binary fields in tool args (mara).

diego: created PR: github.com/redwood/sdk-go/pull/314 (adds Marshal tests + fix). Will push hotfix tag in next 2 hrs.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch sdk-go-hotfix -> staging (owner: diego).

mara: I sent the workaround to Acme, they confirmed they can implement base64 field quickly. They want ETA for official SDK release.

diego: ETA for release with hotfix: ~4 hours to cut RC, 24 hours for general release after bake. I'll update ticket. :white_check_mark:

jordan: also adding integration test to our CI that runs through runtime validation + clients (py/ts/go) with edgecases: null bytes, arrays, nested objects.

mara: thanks everyone — marking this as in-progress on the ticket. Will follow-up once hotfix is out and customer confirms.
